newsitem.title: CANADA: Sikorsky to bid for Canadian helicopters.
newsitem.headline: Sikorsky to bid for Canadian helicopters.

text.p: Sikorsky Aircraft Corp, a unit of United Technologies Corp, said on Monday it teamed up with several Canadian companies to compete for a government contract to provide new search-and-rescue helicopters.

The team will include CAE Inc 's CAE Aviation unit of Edmonton, Alberta, Canadian Marconi Co, Litton Systems of Toronto, GE Canada, a unit of General Electric Co, and IMP Aerospace of Halifax, Nova Scotia, Sikorsky said.
The team will compete for the government program with a version of Sikorsky's S-70A Black Hawk helicopter.

Canada's Defense Minister David Collenette said last year that his government had approved the procurement of up to 15 new search-and-rescue helicopters. The helicopters are expected to cost about C$600 million if bought outright. Funds for the purchase were already provided for in the federal budget, Collenette said.
The government was expected to release its final specifications for the helicopters by the end of October or November, a Sikorsky spokesman said.

The new helicopters will replace the aging group of CH133 Labrador helicopters which have been in service since 1963. If a contract is signed by the end of this year, deliveries of the new helicopters should start by 1998 and conclude by October 2001.
